text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Leftist PDS leader Massimo D'Alema renewed his call for an agreement with the opposition to set up a bi-cameral commission to carry out constitutional reforms (all).

* The cabinet is expected to discuss tomorrow a planned reform of Italy's legal system put forward by Justice Minister Giovanni Maria Flick. Flick's draft changes would allow defendants facing jail terms of up to three years to negotiate sentences but a very controversial point is whether they have to admit guilt in order to benefit from the new system (all).

* An extra mini-budget seems nearer as undersecretary to the Prime minister Enrico Micheli said "it is a possibility" and added the government may decide to intervene before March. Micheli added this budget would be "balanced" and underlined the need for more cuts to public expenditures (all).
* Labour Minister Tiziano Treu met with Prime Minister Romano Prodi to discuss the row over metalworkers contract renewal as trade unions confirmed the decision to hold 10 hours of strikes (all).

* Italian inflation remained steady in December at 2.6 percent year-on-year, the lowest level since June 1969. Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi says government's 1997 inflation target of 2.5 percent is "within reach" but January CPI is expected to worsen a bit (all).
* Italy new car registrations in December are expected to show a slight rise on December 1995 to 105,000 units from 98,959. Official figures are due out on January 10 (Sole 24 Ore).
* EA-Generali, which leads an international group of bidders for the privatisation of Austrian Creditanstalt said it had increased its offer for the bank (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
